title: Identification of risk factors and (bio)markers of taxane-induced chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy in patients with ovarian and breast cancer
summary:
Chemotherapy with taxanes is an important part of the treatment for breast and ovarian cancer. Unfortunately, this therapy can sometimes cause a side effect called chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN). CIPN often leads to tingling or numbness in the hands and feet, as well as pain and problems with coordination. Since there is currently no specific treatment to prevent or cure CIPN, early detection is very important.

The aim of this study is to identify risk factors and biomarkers that could allow an earlier diagnosis of CIPN. We are investigating whether certain proteins in the blood can provide clues about the development and severity of nerve damage. In the future, this could help identify patients who are at higher risk and enable more personalized treatment strategies.

interventions.name:
Monocentric prospective cohort study conducted at the University Medical Center Mainz with three assessment time points: T0 = before initiation of taxane therapy (baseline), T1 = before cycle 2, and T2 = four weeks after completion of taxane therapy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Ovarian or breast cancer with planned taxane-based chemotherapy
Exclusion criteria:
Inflammatory diseases of the central nervous system, history of acute vascular events (hemorrhage/ischemia), acute polyneuropathy, neurodegenerative disorders, prior treatment with taxanes, or impaired capacity to provide informed consent
